resolution.exact_formula_verbatim: Ratio of earnings after interest, dividends, and taxes but before depreciation to book assets
resolution.evidence_for_formula_choice: The paper's only formal definition of Cash Flow appears in Appendix A, Table A1 (p.551): "Ratio of earnings after interest, dividends, and taxes but before depreciation to book assets". Parsing this phrase term by term: "earnings" starts at operating income before depreciation (OIBDP); "after interest" subtracts interest expense (XINT); "after taxes" subtracts income taxes (TXT); "after dividends" subtracts common dividends (DVC); "but before depreciation" instructs that depreciation (DP) is NOT subtracted -- i.e., we stop at OIBDP rather than going down to operating income after depreciation. The denominator "book assets" is total assets (AT). This maps exactly to Formula A: (OIBDP - XINT - TXT - DVC) / AT. Formula B = (IB + DP) / AT is incorrect because it implicitly adds back depreciation to net income but does NOT subtract common dividends, contradicting "after ... dividends". Formula C = OIBDP / AT is incorrect because it does not subtract interest, taxes, or dividends, contradicting "after interest, dividends, and taxes". Note that the paper additionally states (p.536, Section 3.3): "We follow the literature (Bates et al., 2009; Opler et al., 1999) in our empirical testing and control for several variables that affect firm cash policy." The Table A1 phrasing is itself the standard Bates-Stulz-Opler cash flow construction phrasing, which the paper has imported verbatim without restatement of the underlying Compustat line items.
resolution.why_sd_mismatches: The formula identification (Formula A) is correct; the SD discrepancy is NOT a formula problem -- it is a sample-composition problem compounded by winsorization. Three points from the paper drive this: (1) Section 3.3 (p.536): "We winsorize all variables at the 1st and 99th percentiles to minimize the influence of outliers." This applies to Cash Flow. The user's reported Formula-A SD ~31 is consistent with a sample that has NOT had the 1%/99% winsorization applied to Cash Flow, or has been winsorized but on a larger sample that includes more extreme-CF firms. (2) The prior gap analysis (Task 4) showed the user's verbatim-filter sample is 81,482 vs the paper's 56,646 -- a 24,836-obs gap. Those extra observations are concentrated in small/young firms with missing controls; these are exactly the firm-years where CF/AT takes extreme values (numerator can be many multiples of small AT). Filtering down to all-controls-non-missing eliminates most of these extreme observations and shrinks SD dramatically. (3) The shape of the paper's Table 1 distribution itself confirms heavy left-tail influence even post-winsorization: median = 0.0684 (positive), p25 = -0.0150 (near zero), p75 = 0.1210 (positive), but mean = -0.3758 (far below p25) and SD = 4.8386 (~35x the IQR of 0.136). This is the signature of 1%/99% winsorization applied to a CF/AT distribution where the 1st-percentile value (the cap) is itself very negative -- i.e., the winsorization cap, multiplied by ~566 observations (1% of 56,646), pulls the mean down to -0.38 and inflates SD to ~5. The user's SD ~31 indicates the cap is even more extreme in the user's larger 81,482-obs sample because the missing-control firms have more extreme CF tails. Resolution: applying the implicit all-controls-non-missing filter (from Task 4) BEFORE the 1%/99% winsorization should bring SD into the 4-6 range.
resolution.paper_cites_other_source_for_cf_formula: Bates et al. (2009); Opler et al. (1999)
resolution.conclusive_construction_method: From the paper's own text, the construction can be specified only as follows: (Step 1) Compute Cash Flow_{i,t} = (OIBDP - XINT - TXT - DVC) / AT for each firm-year, per the verbatim Table A1 definition "Ratio of earnings after interest, dividends, and taxes but before depreciation to book assets". (Step 2) Apply the full regression-sample filters from Section 3.1: 1997-2015, drop SIC 4900-4999 and SIC 6000-6999, drop AT <= 0 or missing. (Step 3) Apply the implicit all-controls-non-missing filter implied by Section 3.3's list of controls (Firm Size, Firm Age, Book Leverage, Market-to-book, Cash Flow, Capital Expenditure, Acquisition Expenditure, Dividend Paying Firms(0/1), R&D Expenditure, Net Working Capital, Industry Cash Flow Volatility). (Step 4) Apply the explicit winsorization from Section 3.3: "We winsorize all variables at the 1st and 99th percentiles to minimize the influence of outliers." WHAT IS MISSING FROM THE PAPER: (a) The paper does not specify the exact Compustat field names or formula at the line-item level -- it relies on natural-language phrasing that the reader must back out to (OIBDP - XINT - TXT - DVC) / AT. (b) The paper does not state whether the denominator AT is contemporaneous (AT_t) or beginning-of-year (AT_{t-1}). The Cash variable uses BoY AT explicitly ("scaled by total book assets at the beginning of the year"), but the Cash Flow definition omits any timing qualifier on "book assets". This is a genuine ambiguity. (c) The paper does not state whether Table 1 reports pre- or post-winsorize statistics; convention in the literature is post-winsorize, but the paper does not say so. (d) The paper does not state whether winsorization is performed firm-by-firm, year-by-year, pooled across the full panel, or by industry; the sentence "at the 1st and 99th percentiles" is silent on the partition. (e) The paper references an Online Appendix (footnote 7, p.537: "The Online Appendix is available at https://sites.google.com/site/mockeefe/Data.") which may contain the missing operational details, but the paper itself does not restate them. To replicate the paper's exact Cash Flow distribution from the published text alone is therefore not possible; the Online Appendix at the URL above must be consulted, or the authors contacted, for the four points (b)-(d) listed.
